summary: Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating prodrug activated by hepatic CYP450 to cytotoxic metabolites that cross-link DNA. It treats lymphomas, leukemias, multiple myeloma and several solid tumors, pediatric minimal-change nephrotic syndrome, and is used (off-label) as an immunosuppressant in severe autoimmune disease. Major toxicities are myelosuppression, hemorrhagic cystitis (mitigated by hydration and mesna), cardiotoxicity at high doses, infertility and secondary malignancy.
indications: Malignant lymphomas (Hodgkin disease, lymphocytic, mixed-cell, histiocytic, Burkitt lymphoma)
Leukemias (chronic lymphocytic, chronic granulocytic, acute myelogenous/monocytic, acute lymphoblastic)
Adenocarcinoma of the ovary and breast carcinoma
Biopsy-proven minimal change nephrotic syndrome in children who fail or cannot tolerate corticosteroids
Off-label: severe lupus nephritis, ANCA-associated vasculitis and other refractory autoimmune disease

dosage.d: 40-50 mg/kg IV in divided doses over 2-5 days
dosage.n: Give in the morning with hydration

dosage.d: 10-15 mg/kg IV every 7-10 days, or 3-5 mg/kg twice weekly

dosage.n: Max cumulative 168 mg/kg; >90 days raises male sterility risk

dosage.d: e.g. 500-1000 mg/m2 IV monthly (varies by protocol)

admin: Administer in the morning and force diuresis with adequate oral or IV fluids during and after dosing to reduce urinary tract toxicity
Reconstitute lyophilized powder per label; inspect for melting (temperature-sensitive)
Handle and dispose as a hazardous cytotoxic agent
Consider mesna and aggressive hydration with high-dose IV regimens to prevent hemorrhagic cystitis
Antiemetic prophylaxis is recommended; monitor blood counts before each cycle
moa: Cyclophosphamide is a prodrug metabolized by hepatic cytochrome P450 (CYP2B6, 2A6, 3A, 2C9, 2C19) to active alkylating metabolites (notably phosphoramide mustard). These form covalent cross-links between and within DNA strands, preventing DNA replication and triggering apoptosis of rapidly proliferating cells. The same action suppresses immune effector cells, giving its immunosuppressive effect.

absolute: Severe hypersensitivity to cyclophosphamide or its metabolites (anaphylaxis, cross-reactivity with other alkylating agents)
relative: Pre-existing myelosuppression or active severe infection
Prior pelvic irradiation or doxorubicin exposure

preg: Contraindicated. Cyclophosphamide can cause fetal harm including malformations and fetal death. Advise patients of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and after treatment (per label, women for 1 year and men for at least 4 months after the last dose).
lact: Cyclophosphamide is excreted in human milk; breastfeeding is contraindicated during and for a period after treatment because of the potential for serious adverse effects (neutropenia) in the infant.
renal: Active metabolites are renally cleared and the drug is dialyzable; reduce dose and ensure adequate hydration in renal impairment to limit accumulation and urotoxicity.
hepatic: Hepatic activation is required, but significant hepatic impairment can reduce activation and increase toxicity; dose reduction may be warranted. Veno-occlusive liver disease can occur, especially at high doses.

major: Other cardiotoxic agents (anthracyclines, trastuzumab, prior chest irradiation) - additive cardiotoxicity at high doses
Live vaccines - risk of disseminated infection in immunosuppressed patients
Other myelosuppressive chemo/radiation - additive marrow suppression
moderate: CYP3A4/2B6 inducers (rifampin, phenobarbital) - increase active metabolite formation/toxicity
CYP inhibitors - may reduce activation or alter clearance
interactions.food: Take oral doses with food; maintain high fluid intake to protect the bladder.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol due to additive nausea and potential hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes leukopenia/thrombocytopenia, hematuria, and may elevate liver enzymes; can suppress immune response to vaccines.

serious: Severe myelosuppression and bone marrow failure with serious infections
Hemorrhagic cystitis, pyelitis, ureteritis and hematuria
Cardiotoxicity - myocarditis, myopericarditis, arrhythmias, congestive heart failure (high dose)
Pulmonary toxicity - pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis, veno-occlusive disease

monitoring: Complete blood count (especially neutrophils and platelets) frequently, before each course
Urinalysis for hematuria and signs of cystitis
Cardiac monitoring (ECG, signs of heart failure), especially with high-dose regimens
Serum sodium (SIADH); pregnancy status before treatment
counsel: Drink plenty of fluids and empty the bladder frequently; report pink/red urine or painful urination immediately
Use effective contraception during and after treatment; discuss fertility preservation
Report fever, sore throat, bruising or bleeding (low blood counts)
Expect possible hair loss; it usually regrows after treatment
Avoid live vaccines and report shortness of breath or chest symptoms
pk: Requires hepatic activation; cytotoxic effect over days
Parent drug plasma peak shortly after dosing (linear kinetics)
Metabolite effects persist; marrow nadir ~7-14 days
Store vials at or below 25 C; avoid heat (powder can melt)
pearls: Hemorrhagic cystitis is the hallmark urinary toxicity - prevent with vigorous hydration, morning dosing and mesna at high doses
High-dose cyclophosphamide is cardiotoxic (myopericarditis, CHF) - watch in patients with cardiac risk or prior anthracyclines
Causes dose-dependent infertility; treatment beyond 90 days markedly increases male sterility
Secondary malignancy (notably bladder cancer and MDS/leukemia) is a long-term risk
Can cause SIADH with hyponatremia, especially at high doses with fluid loading
missed: For oral therapy, contact the oncology team rather than self-adjusting; take a missed oral dose only as advised. Do not take a double dose. IV doses are given on schedule by clinicians.
overdose: Overdose intensifies myelosuppression, urotoxicity, cardiotoxicity and veno-occlusive disease. There is no specific antidote; cyclophosphamide is dialyzable. Manage with supportive care, hematologic support, mesna and hydration for the bladder, and treat infections and cardiac/hepatic complications.
